name: DistributedLock
purpose: Named mutex with lease expiry that grants one holder exclusive access across processes and is released explicitly or by lease timeout on crash.
invariants: At most one caller MUST hold a given resource_id at a time; try_lock on a held lock returns None.
Locks ALWAYS auto release after lease_s elapses so a crashed holder CANNOT deadlock the resource forever.
Unlock with a non matching owner_id MUST be rejected so callers cannot release locks they do not own.
lease_s MUST be positive; a zero or negative lease SHALL raise a configuration error.
The primitive NEVER guarantees fairness across callers beyond the single holder invariant.
extension_contract: Swap backends by implementing DistributedLock as an adapter (Redis SET NX PX, etcd lease, Consul session) and register it as a component; higher guarantees (fencing tokens) plug in by wrapping try_lock in a middleware that annotates the handle.
consumption_example:
async def with_critical_section(lock: DistributedLock, resource: str, owner: str) -> bool:
    handle = await lock.try_lock(resource, owner, lease_s=30)
    if handle is None:
        return False
    try:
        return True
    finally:
        await lock.unlock(handle)

sources.source: Dapr 1.14 Distributed Lock building block overview

why_essential: Coordinating rare sequential work across workers (backfills, leader only cron) needs one contract; scattering ad hoc Redis SETNX code loses lease semantics and owner checks.
alternatives_considered: Advisory Postgres locks which tie correctness to one database and one transaction
Quorum based leader election which solves a bigger problem and is often overkill
